Hilary Charlesworth.title: Hilary Charlesworth
Hilary Charlesworth.desc: Australian legal academic and judge of the International Court of Justice
Hilary Charlesworth.extract: Hilary Christiane Mary Charlesworth is an Australian international lawyer. She has been a Judge of the International Court of Justice since 5 November 2021, and is Harrison Moore Professor of Law and Melbourne Laureate Professor at the University of Melbourne, and Distinguished Professor at the Australian National University.

Lassa Oppenheim.title: Lassa Oppenheim
Lassa Oppenheim.extract: Lassa Francis Lawrence Oppenheim was a German jurist. He has been characterized as the father of the modern discipline of international law, especially the hard legal positivist school of thought. His two-volume International Law: A Treatise has influenced international law. He inspired Joseph Raz and Prosper Weil.

Lord Arnold McNair.title: Arnold McNair, 1st Baron McNair
Lord Arnold McNair.extract: Arnold Duncan McNair, 1st Baron McNair was a British jurist and judge of the International Court of Justice and later the first president of the European Court of Human Rights.

Mielville W. Fuller.title: Melville Fuller
Mielville W. Fuller.desc: Chief Justice of the United States from 1888 to 1910
Mielville W. Fuller.extract: Melville Weston Fuller was an American politician, attorney, and jurist who served as the eighth chief justice of the United States from 1888 until his death in 1910. Staunch conservatism marked his tenure on the Supreme Court, exhibited by his tendency to support unfettered free enterprise and to oppose broad federal power. He wrote major opinions on the federal income tax, the Commerce Clause, a

Dame Hazel Fox.extract: Hazel Mary Fox CMG KC, often known as Lady Fox, was a British international lawyer and an expert in State Immunity. She was involved in a number of British high profile cases where individuals had legal disputes with governments.

A. Beernaert.extract: Auguste Marie François Beernaert was the prime minister of Belgium from October 1884 to March 1894, and the 1909 Nobel Peace Prize laureate.

Guenter Heinz Treitel.extract: Sir Guenter Heinz Treitel was a German-born English academic and Vinerian Professor of English Law.

Sir Cecil Hurst.title: Cecil Hurst
Sir Cecil Hurst.extract: Sir Cecil James Barrington Hurst, GCMG, KCB, QC was a British international lawyer. He worked from 1929 to 1945 as a judge to the Permanent Court of International Justice in The Hague, serving from 1934 to 1936 as president of the court.

Wilhelm Wundt.title: Wilhelm Wundt
Wilhelm Wundt.extract: Wilhelm Maximilian Wundt was a German physiologist, philosopher, professor, and one of the fathers of modern psychology. Wundt, who distinguished psychology as a science from philosophy and biology, was the first person to call himself a psychologist.

Sir John Sparrow.title: John Sparrow (academic)
Sir John Sparrow.extract: John Hanbury Angus Sparrow OBE was an English academic, barrister, book-collector, and Warden of All Souls College, Oxford, from 1952 to 1977.

Rolv Ryssdal.title: Rolv Ryssdal

Van Eysinga.title: Willem van Eysinga
Van Eysinga.extract: Willem Jan Mari van Eysinga was a Dutch diplomat and jurist. He served as a judge on the Permanent Court of International Justice from 1931 to 1945.

Shigeru Oda.title: Shigeru Oda
Shigeru Oda.extract: Shigeru Oda  was a Japanese jurist who was a judge on the International Court of Justice from 1976 until 2003, when he retired. He served as vice-president from 1991 to 1994. His main area of expertise was law of the sea. He was born in Sapporo.

A. Pearce Higgins.title: Alexander Pearce Higgins
A. Pearce Higgins.extract: Alexander Pearce Higgins was a British international law scholar. He was Whewell Professor of International Law at the University of Cambridge (1920–1935), President of the Institut de Droit International (1929–1931), and a member of the Permanent Court of Arbitration (1930–1935).

G. C. Cheshire.title: Geoffrey Cheshire
G. C. Cheshire.extract: Geoffrey Chevalier Cheshire  was a British barrister and legal scholar. He was the father of Leonard Cheshire, the British war hero and founder of the Cheshire Foundation Homes for the Sick.

Ernst Rabel.title: Ernst Rabel
Ernst Rabel.extract: Ernst Rabel was an Austrian-born scholar of Roman law, German private law, and comparative law, who, as the founding director of the Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Foreign and International Private Law, in Berlin, achieved international recognition in the period between the World Wars, before being forced into retirement under the Nazi regime, and immigrating to the United States, in 1939. Malgosia Fitzmaurice.extract: Malgosia A. Fitzmaurice is a Polish lawyer who is professor of public international law at Queen Mary University of London. She is an international lawyer with a specialist interest in marine environmental matters, the law of treaties, and indigenous peoples.

Sir Gerald Fitzmaurice.title: Gerald Fitzmaurice
Sir Gerald Fitzmaurice.extract: Sir Gerald Gray Fitzmaurice was an English barrister and judge. Julio Sanguinetti.title: Julio María Sanguinetti
Julio Sanguinetti.extract: Julio María Sanguinetti Coirolo often known by his initials JMS, is a Uruguayan former lawyer, journalist and politician of the Colorado Party (PC) who served as the President of Uruguay as the 35th president from 1985 to 1990, and again as the 37th president from 1995 to 2000. Sir Eric Beckett.extract: Sir William Eric Beckett, KCMG, QC was a British international lawyer who served as Legal Adviser to the Foreign Office from 1945 to 1953.

Sir Michael Wood.extract: Sir Michael Charles Wood is a member of the International Law Commission. He also practices as a barrister from chambers at 20 Essex Street, in London.

Hisashi Owada.extract: Hisashi Owada  is a Japanese jurist, diplomat and professor of law. He is the father of Empress Masako and the father-in-law of the reigning Emperor of Japan, Naruhito.

F. A. Mann.title: Frederick Alexander Mann
F. A. Mann.extract: Frederick Alexander Mann, CBE, FBA, QC (Hon.) also known as Francis Mann was a German-born British jurist. A solicitor in private practice for most of his career, he was nevertheless one of the most influential legal scholars of his generation, being a noted authority on international law and the law of money.

Sir Frank Berman.title: Frank Berman
Sir Frank Berman.extract: Sir Franklin Delow Berman, is a British barrister and leading authority in international law. He was Legal Adviser to the Foreign and Commonwealth Office from 1991 to 1999.

Edouard Rolin Jaequemyns.extract: Edouard Gustave Marie Rolin-Jaequemyns (1863–1936) was a Belgian jurist, diplomat and politician. He served as Belgian Minister of the Interior between 1925 and 1926, as a member of the Permanent Court of Arbitration between 1928 and 1930, and as a judge at the Permanent Court of International Justice between 1931 and 1936. He was the son of Gustave Rolin-Jaequemyns and the cousin of Henri Rolin.

Sir Ian Brownlie.extract: Sir Ian Brownlie, was an English barrister and academic, specialising in international law. He was Chichele Professor of Public International Law from 1980 to 1999.

Jean d'Aspremont.extract: Jean Marie Gobert Count d'Aspremont Lynden is a lawyer and professor of international legal theory at Sciences Po in Paris, at the University of Manchester and at the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies in Geneva.

Lord Finlay of Nairn.title: Robert Finlay, 1st Viscount Finlay
Lord Finlay of Nairn.extract: Robert Bannatyne Finlay, 1st Viscount Finlay,, known as Sir Robert Finlay from 1895 to 1916, was a British barrister and politician who was Lord High Chancellor of Great Britain from 1916 to 1919.

He was a widely traveled authority on law, government, and history whose expertise led to high political offices, culminating with his successful role as ambassador to the United States from 1907 to 1913. Roberto Ago.title: Roberto Ago
Roberto Ago.extract: Roberto Ago was an Italian jurist. He served as a judge on the International Court of Justice from 1979 until 1995. He was Professor of International Law at the Universities of Catania (1934–1935), Genoa (1935–1938), and finally Rome (1956–1982). He specialized in both private and public international law.

Sir Derek Bowett.title: Derek Bowett
Sir Derek Bowett.extract: Sir Derek William Bowett, was an international lawyer and academic. He was appointed Whewell Professor of International Law in 1981 and was President of Queens' College, Cambridge 1970–1982.

Sir George Sherston Baker.title: George Sherston Baker
Sir George Sherston Baker.extract: Sir George Edward Dunstan Sherston Baker, 4th Baronet was a British barrister and judge. He was a County Court judge from 1901 until his death. He was also a prolific writer on legal topics.

Friederich von Martens.title: Friedrich Martens
Friederich von Martens.extract: Friedrich Fromhold Martens, or Friedrich Fromhold von Martens, was a diplomat and jurist in service of the Russian Empire who made important contributions to the science of international law. He represented Russia at the Hague Peace Conferences and helped to settle the first cases of international arbitration, notably the dispute between France and the United Kingdom over Newfoundland. Lord Phillimore.title: Walter Phillimore, 1st Baron Phillimore
Lord Phillimore.extract: Walter George Frank Phillimore, 1st Baron Phillimore, known as Sir Walter Phillimore, 2nd Baronet, from 1885 to 1918, was a British lawyer and judge.
